 Set as preferred source Listen Summarise SPF website e-services were down for about three hours because of technical issues, stopping police reports through the portal.
 Police said at 4.28pm that the website was back to normal and the technical issues had been resolved.
 The outage follows recent global tech problems, including a Microsoft outage and earlier website shutdowns linked to flaws in PHP.
 AI generated
 SINGAPORE – E-services on the Singapore Police Force’s (SPF) website were not available for about three hours on Nov 16 because of technical issues.
 In a post on Facebook at 4.28pm, the police said the website had returned to normal and that they can now receive police reports via the e-services portal.
 They said the technical issues that had affected the website have been resolved.
 In an earlier post at 12.50pm, the police said the SPF website was experiencing intermittent connectivity, and that they were unable to receive police reports via the e-services portal.
 The police advised the public to call 999 for urgent police assistance or the police hotline on 1800-255-0000 for other matters.
 This comes after a series of global tech issues over the past weeks.
 Last week, a Microsoft outage disrupted e-mail services across organisations in Singapore , including in the government and banking sectors. The outage also paralysed government offices, traders and businesses around the world.
 In October, governments and companies globally shut down websites after artificial intelligence uncovered critical flaws in a widely used programming language called PHP.
